The main critiques of using the IAEA as a model for international AI governance include:

1. The IAEA's own historical enforcement challenges, which raise concerns about its effectiveness in a new context (A. Wasil, 2024).
2. The difficulty of monitoring and controlling diffuse, rapidly evolving software compared to tangible nuclear materials (Cha, 2024; Chesterman, 2021; Law & Ho, 2024).
3. The speed of AI development outpacing institutional responses (Hausenloy & Dennis, 2023).
4. The prominent role of non-state actors in AI, which complicates governance (Hausenloy & Dennis, 2023; Zaidi & Dafoe, 2021).
5. The current lack of international consensus on AI risks, contrasting with the unified response to the atomic bombing of Hiroshima (Bodini, 2024; Chesterman, 2021; A. Wasil, 2024).
